stories.headline: Jets list seven inactives for Sunday’s game at Chicago, including Hall and Mitchell
stories.summary: The Jets posted seven inactives about 90 minutes before the 1 p.m. kickoff at Soldier Field: edge Kingsley Enagbare, running back Breece Hall, linebacker Kiko Mauigoa, wide receiver Adonai Mitchell, guard Dylan Parham, tight end Mason Taylor, and defensive back Nahshon Wright. Wide receiver Sterling Shepard and linebacker Jaden Keller were elevated from the practice squad. Kicker Jason Sanders, elevated for the first three games, was signed to the active roster Tuesday. Chicago’s inactive list includes quarterback Caleb Williams. Kickoff is on FOX.

stories.headline: Mario Lemieux joins Crosby for the Penguins’ 60th-anniversary puck drop
stories.summary: Before Saturday’s home opener against Montreal, Mario Lemieux walked onto the ice at PPG Paints Arena for a ceremonial puck drop marking the Penguins’ 60th anniversary season. Doug McGregor, son of original owner Jack McGregor, and chairman Jeff Hoffman joined him. Sidney Crosby and Canadiens captain Nick Suzuki met at center ice, and the original puck from the franchise’s first home game in 1967 was brought back out. The matchup itself echoed that 1967 opener against Montreal. Lemieux fist-bumped players on the bench as the crowd gave the Hall of Famer a standing ovation.

stories.headline: Trump tells Ohio voters the polls don’t account for him campaigning
stories.summary: At Saturday’s Vandalia, Ohio rally, President Trump said Republicans will overcome soft polls now that he is on the trail personally. “These fake polls, they don’t account for one thing. They don’t account for the fact that Trump is out campaigning,” he told the crowd, urging them to pretend he is on the ballot. A recent Fox News poll gives Democrats a wider House path, projecting 215 Democratic seats to 201 Republican with 19 toss-ups still in play. A House GOP memo obtained by Fox says the final four weeks will focus on the border, fraudulent use of taxpayer dollars, the economy, and public safety.

stories.headline: Trump creates a Super Intelligence Force led by DNI Clayton and FTC’s Ferguson
stories.summary: On Sunday morning President Trump announced a Super Intelligence Force to follow the White House Accord on Super Intelligence. He said the group will coordinate federal engagement with consumers, public-interest groups, religious organizations, critical-infrastructure providers, and AI companies so America keeps leading what he called bigger than the industrial revolution and the internet. Leaders named include Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton, FTC Chairman Andrew Ferguson, Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering and CTO Emil Michael, and OPM Director Scott Kupor, reporting to Trump and Chief of Staff Susie Wiles.

stories.headline: Trump credits pharma tariffs after Bayer announces a $2.2 billion Ohio campus
stories.summary: President Trump said Bayer announced a new $2.2 billion pharmaceutical manufacturing campus near Columbus that will create thousands of Ohio jobs in advanced manufacturing, research, and construction. He credited his pharmaceutical tariffs for more than $600 billion in new pharma investment and lower most-favored-nation drug prices, writing that companies must build in America, hire American workers, and price drugs fairly for patients—or pay. The Truth Social post landed as Trump campaigned in Ohio for the midterms.

stories.headline: Supreme Court opens a new term with guns, voting, and Trump power still on the docket
stories.summary: Chief Justice John Roberts opens the Court’s new term Monday with oral arguments, starting with a climate-liability fight against oil and gas companies. Already on the docket are religious-school preschool aid, state AR-15-style bans, and proof-of-citizenship voting rules. Fox notes the 6-3 majority has greenlighted many Trump emergency applications while also handing him losses on tariffs and birthright citizenship. Gallup has Court approval at a record-low 33 percent, and justices have warned Congress about rising threats, including a swatting incident at Justice Barrett’s home.

stories.headline: Fugitive in a 2009 silicone-injection murder is caught after a DMV license renewal
stories.summary: Tamaira Angell Smith, 52, faces a felony murder charge in the 2009 death of Eyanna Moore, 29, after an illegal silicone injection in a Georgia hotel room. Police said Smith fled after a 2009 warrant, later obtained a South Carolina license under a stolen identity, and in July 2026 called the DMV for help renewing it when an online alert blocked her. Facial recognition tied her to the murder warrant; Texas police arrested her in McKinney in August and she was extradited to Gwinnett County. A bond hearing is set for Oct. 22.

stories.headline: Metallica plays ‘Devil’s Dance’ for the first time in 18 years at Sphere night two
stories.summary: On Saturday’s second Life Burns Faster show at Las Vegas Sphere, Metallica opened with Blackened, Fuel, and Leper Messiah, then played Devil’s Dance for the first time since June 7, 2008. The Outlaw Torn also returned for the first time since 2019. The residency’s No Repeat Weekend format keeps Thursday and Saturday setlists entirely different across 24 dates through March 13, 2027. Fan video of the deep cuts circulated quickly Sunday morning.

stories.headline: Carolina Renaissance Festival opens its 33rd season in Huntersville
stories.summary: The Carolina Renaissance Festival kicked off Oct. 3 at 16445 Poplar Tent Road in Huntersville, North Carolina. Rain-or-shine weekends run Saturdays and Sundays from 9:30 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. through Nov. 22, with horseback jousting, circus entertainers, rides, artisan demonstrations, shopping, and games. The “Escape to the Renaissance” return marks the fair’s 33rd annual season.

stories.headline: Westport–Weston Restaurant Week runs Oct. 4–18 with 20 prix-fixe menus
stories.summary: The Westport-Weston Chamber’s Restaurant Week is actually two weeks, Sunday Oct. 4 through Oct. 18, with nineteen Westport restaurants and one Southport spot posting prix-fixe lunch and dinner deals. Chamber president Matthew Mandell said the point is to eat local and show off Fairfield County’s dining scene. Participating names include The Boathouse at Saugatuck, Kawa Ni, Zucca Gastrobar, Felice, Pepe’s, Romanacci, and Yuzu. Trumbull’s own town newsflash had nothing newer than already-archived items, so this nearby free stand-in is labeled honestly.

stories.headline: Trump blasts Fox & Friends for skipping his packed midterm rallies
stories.summary: In a Sunday morning Truth Social post, President Trump said Fox & Friends was not covering sold-out rallies in Ohio, Alabama, Texas, and Oklahoma and warned MAGA viewers would “very quickly stop watching.” He attacked Jessica Tarlov and said Fox spends more time talking to “Communists, Socialists, and Dumocrats” without rebuttal. He also criticized Maria Bartiromo’s exit and reminded Fox it “almost went out of business” the last time it tried this before an election. Mediaite noted Fox & Friends had aired a brief data-center clip from the Ohio rally minutes earlier.

stories.headline: Twisted Sister box set collects the classic 1982–1987 studio albums
stories.summary: BMG and Rhino announced Totally Twisted - The Studio Albums 1982-1987, a five-LP color vinyl and five-CD set spanning Under The Blade, You Can’t Stop Rock ’N’ Roll, Stay Hungry, Come Out And Play, and Love Is For Suckers. The package covers the Dee Snider–era run that produced We’re Not Gonna Take It and I Wanna Rock. It arrives as Sebastian Bach fronts the band on fall dates after Snider stepped aside for health reasons, with Jay Jay French and Eddie Ojeda still on guitar.

stories.headline: Harley-Davidson’s Ladies International Run brings about 400 bikes to Pescara
stories.summary: About 400 Harley-Davidson motorcycles and roughly 900 riders filled Pescara, Italy, on Oct. 3 for the International Ladies of Harley Run, part of the brand’s 2026 European community calendar with Jeep. The weekend included a city parade and fundraising tied to cancer research. Organizers billed it as one of the partnership’s fall stops before a H.O.G. Winter Meeting later in Genoa.

stories.headline: Floor Jansen’s solo album Hytress aims for a heavier sound that isn’t Nightwish
stories.summary: Nightwish singer Floor Jansen told Finland’s Imperiumi that her second solo album, Hytress, due Jan. 15, 2027 via REVAMP Music/Warner, pushes a heavier, more compact metal sound inspired by bands like Bleed From Within, Gojira, and Periphery—without copying Nightwish’s orchestral bombast. She said the twelve-song set keeps catchy choruses under a “very heavy jacket,” and that Nightwish’s current live pause lets her tour the heavier material without clashing setlists. Paragon, her 2023 solo debut, has nearly 150 million streams.
